# Measures of spread - Practice Test - Year 10A

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes. To find quartiles, split the ordered data at the median; when there is an odd number of values, leave the median out of both halves. Use the population standard deviation ($\sigma$) and round it to two decimal places.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

The data set is 14, 9, 21, 17, 30, 12.

(a) Find the range.

(b) Find the median.

**Question 2**

The number of books read by 11 students over the holidays was:

3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, 20

(a) Write the five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile $Q_1$, median, upper quartile $Q_3$, maximum).

(b) Find the interquartile range (IQR).

**Question 3**

Name the measure of spread described in each statement.

(a) The difference between the highest and lowest values.

(b) The spread of the middle 50% of the data.

(c) A measure based on how far, on average, the values are from the mean.

**Question 4**

A box plot of a data set shows: minimum 20, lower quartile 35, median 42, upper quartile 50, maximum 70.

(a) Find the range.

(b) Find the IQR.

(c) What percentage of the values lie between 35 and 50?

(d) What percentage of the values are above 42?

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

The ages of the 12 members of a community choir are:

18, 21, 22, 25, 27, 30, 31, 33, 36, 40, 44, 52

(a) Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$ and the IQR.

(b) A value is an outlier if it is more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ below $Q_1$ or more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ above $Q_3$. Is the age 52 an outlier? Show your working.

**Question 6**

Ten students recorded the number of minutes they spent on homework one night:

2, 15, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 48

(a) Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$ and the IQR.

(b) Find the lower and upper fences, $Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ and $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.

(c) Which values are outliers?

**Question 7**

A data set is 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 20.

(a) Find the range, the IQR and the standard deviation.

(b) The value 20 is replaced by 60. Find the new range, IQR and standard deviation.

(c) Which measure of spread was not affected by the change? Explain why.

**Question 8**

The scores of 15 players in a computer game are shown in this stem-and-leaf plot, where 2 | 4 means 24.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 2 | 4 7 9 |
| 3 | 1 3 3 6 8 |
| 4 | 0 2 5 7 |
| 5 | 1 8 |
| 6 | 3 |

(a) Find the median.

(b) Find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.

(c) Find the IQR and the range.

**Question 9**

For each data set, say which measure of spread (range, IQR or standard deviation) is most suitable, and explain why.

(a) The weekly incomes of 200 households in a suburb, where most incomes are moderate but a few are extremely high (strongly positively skewed).

(b) The heights of 500 adult women, which have a symmetric, bell-shaped distribution with no outliers.

(c) Explain why the range is rarely the best measure of spread for a large data set.

**Question 10**

The lifetimes (in hours) of two brands of torch battery were tested. The five-number summaries are:

| Brand | Minimum | $Q_1$ | Median | $Q_3$ | Maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brand A | 18 | 22 | 25 | 27 | 30 |
| Brand B | 10 | 20 | 26 | 33 | 40 |

(a) Find the IQR for each brand.

(b) Which brand is more consistent? Explain.

(c) A hiker needs batteries she can rely on. Which brand should she choose? Explain using the measures of centre and spread.

**Question 11**

Twenty netball players recorded the number of goals they scored in a match.

| Goals | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 5 | 6 | 3 | 2 | 1 |

(a) Find the median.

(b) Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$ and the IQR.

(c) Find the range.

**Question 12**

Set X: 10, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 50

Set Y: 10, 13, 20, 30, 40, 47, 50

(a) Show that both sets have the same range and the same mean.

(b) Find the IQR of each set.

(c) Explain why the range alone gives a misleading comparison of these two sets.

**Question 13**

A data set is 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. Its distribution is symmetric with no outliers.

(a) Find the IQR.

(b) Find the mean and the standard deviation.

(c) Which measure of spread would you report for this data set? Give a reason.

**Question 14**

Two pizza stores recorded their delivery times over a month.

Store 1: median 28 minutes, IQR 6 minutes

Store 2: median 25 minutes, IQR 18 minutes

(a) Explain what the IQR of 6 minutes tells you about Store 1.

(b) Which store has more predictable delivery times?

(c) Store 2 advertises, "We're faster than Store 1!" Explain why this claim is not the whole story.

**Question 15**

A data set has the five-number summary: minimum 2, $Q_1 = 4$, median 5, $Q_3 = 9$, maximum 20.

(a) Describe the shape of the distribution. Explain how you can tell.

(b) Which measures of centre and spread are most suitable for this data? Explain.

(c) Is the maximum value an outlier? Show your working, using the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule.

**Question 16**

A teacher's test results have a mean of 60, range of 40, IQR of 15 and standard deviation of 9.

(a) The teacher adds 5 bonus marks to every student's result. Copy and complete the "Add 5" column.

(b) Instead, the teacher multiplies every original result by 1.2. Copy and complete the "Multiply by 1.2" column.

| Statistic | Original | Add 5 | Multiply by 1.2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean | 60 | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |
| Range | 40 | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |
| IQR | 15 | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |
| Standard deviation | 9 | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

Two Year 10 classes sat the same test (marks out of 100).

Class P: 45, 52, 55, 58, 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 70, 72, 95

Class Q: 30, 40, 48, 55, 62, 66, 70, 75, 80, 84, 88, 92

(a) Find the five-number summary for each class.

(b) Use the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule to decide whether either class has any outliers.

(c) Which measure of spread is better for comparing the two classes? Explain.

(d) Compare the two classes, referring to centre and spread.

**Question 18**

Eight values, in ascending order, are:

4, 7, 9, 11, 13, $x$, 22, 25

The IQR of the data is 12.

(a) Find $Q_1$.

(b) Find the value of $x$.

(c) Find the median.

(d) Is 25 an outlier? Show your working.

**Question 19**

(a) Write a set of seven whole numbers with a median of 10, a range of 20 and an IQR of 4.

(b) Change one value in your set so that the range becomes 30 but the median and IQR do not change. Write the new set.

(c) What does part (b) show about the range compared with the IQR?

**Question 20**

The annual salaries (in thousands of dollars) of the 10 employees of a small business are:

48, 50, 52, 53, 55, 56, 58, 60, 62, 250

(a) Find the IQR.

(b) Find the standard deviation.

(c) The salary of 250 thousand dollars belongs to the owner. Find the IQR and the standard deviation of the other nine salaries.

(d) Which measure of spread better describes how much the salaries of the business's employees typically vary? Explain using your answers.

# Measures of spread - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) $21$ (b) $15.5$

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) minimum $3$, $Q_1 = 6$, median $10$, $Q_3 = 15$, maximum $20$ (b) $9$

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) range (b) interquartile range (IQR) (c) standard deviation

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) $50$ (b) $15$ (c) $50\%$ (d) $50\%$

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) $Q_1 = 23.5$, $Q_3 = 38$, IQR $= 14.5$ (b) No: the upper fence is $38 + 1.5 \times 14.5 = 59.75$, and $52 < 59.75$.

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) $Q_1 = 17$, $Q_3 = 24$, IQR $= 7$ (b) lower fence $6.5$, upper fence $34.5$ (c) $2$ and $48$

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) range $10$, IQR $6$, standard deviation $3.23$ (b) range $50$, IQR $6$, standard deviation $16.28$ (c) The IQR, because it only uses the middle 50% of the data, so changing the largest value does not affect it.

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) $38$ (b) $Q_1 = 31$, $Q_3 = 47$ (c) IQR $= 16$, range $= 39$

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) IQR, because it is not affected by the few extremely high incomes (outliers or skew). (b) Standard deviation, because the data is symmetric with no outliers, and the standard deviation uses every value. (c) The range depends only on the two most extreme values, so one unusual value can make it very large.

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) Brand A: $5$ hours; Brand B: $13$ hours (b) Brand A, because its IQR (and range) is much smaller. (c) Brand A: its median (25 hours) is almost the same as Brand B's (26 hours), but its lifetimes are much more consistent, and its minimum (18 hours) is much higher than Brand B's (10 hours).

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) $2$ (b) $Q_1 = 1$, $Q_3 = 3$, IQR $= 2$ (c) $5$

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) Both ranges are $50 - 10 = 40$; both means are $\frac{210}{7} = 30$. (b) Set X: $0$; Set Y: $34$ (c) The ranges are equal, but in Set X almost every value is 30, while Set Y's values are spread out. The range only uses the two extreme values.

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) $4$ (b) mean $8$, standard deviation $2.45$ ($\sqrt{6}$) (c) The standard deviation, because the data is symmetric with no outliers, and the standard deviation uses every value.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) The middle 50% of Store 1's delivery times lie within a span of 6 minutes. (b) Store 1 (smaller IQR) (c) Store 2's median time is 3 minutes less, but its IQR is three times as large, so its delivery times vary a lot and many deliveries may take much longer than Store 1's.

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) Positively skewed (skewed to the right): the median is close to $Q_1$, and the upper whisker and upper part of the box are much longer than the lower parts. (b) The median and IQR, because the data is skewed (and has an outlier), and these measures are not affected by extreme values. (c) Yes: IQR $= 5$, upper fence $= 9 + 7.5 = 16.5$, and $20 > 16.5$.

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) Add 5: mean $65$, range $40$, IQR $15$, standard deviation $9$ (b) Multiply by 1.2: mean $72$, range $48$, IQR $18$, standard deviation $10.8$

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) Class P: $45, 56.5, 62.5, 68.5, 95$; Class Q: $30, 51.5, 68, 82, 92$ (b) Class P: IQR $= 12$, fences $38.5$ and $86.5$, so 95 is an outlier. Class Q: IQR $= 30.5$, fences $5.75$ and $127.75$, so no outliers. (c) The IQR, because Class P has an outlier (95), which would make its range and standard deviation larger than the spread of most of the class. (d) Class Q has the higher median (68 compared with 62.5), but Class P's results are much more consistent (IQR 12 compared with 30.5).

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) $Q_1 = 8$ (b) $x = 18$ ($Q_3 = \frac{x + 22}{2} = 20$) (c) $12$ (d) No: the upper fence is $20 + 1.5 \times 12 = 38$, and $25 < 38$.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) For example 0, 8, 8, 10, 12, 12, 20 (accept any set where, in order, the 4th value is 10, the 6th value minus the 2nd value is 4, and the largest minus the smallest is 20) (b) For example 0, 8, 8, 10, 12, 12, 30 (change only the smallest or largest value, keeping it beyond the quartiles) (c) The range depends only on the extreme values, so it can change a lot while the IQR (the middle 50%) does not change at all.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) $8$ thousand dollars ($Q_1 = 52$, $Q_3 = 60$) (b) $58.68$ thousand dollars (c) IQR $8$ thousand dollars ($Q_1 = 51$, $Q_3 = 59$); standard deviation $4.36$ thousand dollars (d) The IQR. It is the same with or without the owner's salary, but the one outlier makes the standard deviation more than 13 times larger, so the standard deviation of all 10 salaries does not describe the typical variation.
check_notes: Five-number summaries (median-split quartiles, median excluded for odd n), IQRs, 1.5 x IQR fences, outliers, ranges, means and population standard deviations recomputed in Python for every data set, including the before and after outlier sets.
